description.narrative: The development impact includes: (i) redeployment of released cash for renewable energy investments in carbon-intensive emerging markets and reduction of GHG emissions, and (ii) strengthening resilience of a critical power generation asset in Armenia, which is expected to enhance reliability of supply, preserve stability of the power system, and facilitate future deployment of renewable energy in the energy mix.

The proposed project involves up to US$150 million debt refinancing package for ContourGlobal Hydro Cascade CJSC (the Company, an existing IFC investee company) in Armenia. In July 2015, the Company acquired the 404.2MW Vorotan cascade hydropower generation plants in southern Armenia, including the 76MW Spandaryan HPP (commissioned in 1989), the 171MW Shamb HPP (commissioned in 1978) and the 157.2MW Tatev HPP (commissioned in 1970) plants along the Vorotan River (together, the Vorotan Cascade). In 2016, IFC arranged a US$140mn financing package to refinance the second instalment of the privatization (#37652, summary of the investment: https://disclosures.ifc.org/project-detail/ESRS/37652/vorotan-debt ). The Vorotan Cascade is among the main power generation complexes in Armenia, providing both peak and base load generation, and performing grid stabilization services. The Vorotan Cascade is supported by a system of four reservoirs: Spandaryan, Angeghakot, Tolors, Shamb and a Tatev daily regulation pond. The new financing is aimed to re-leverage the Company, and through doing so support new modernization investments and free up liquidity for renewable energy (RE) pipeline in emerging markets.

name.narrative: The Project consists of three operational hydropower plants on the Vorotan River in southern Armenia. The Vorotan River flows for 119km through a mountainous area in southern Armenia and then for another 59km through Azerbaijan, before joining the Araks River at the Iran border.
